header: THE THIRD TAB OF THE RAILWAY CARD: THE TRAINS OF THE KOLKATA STATIONS. They start at Howrah (HWH), Sealdah (SDAH), Santragachi (SRC) or Kolkata (KOAA), go over neither Durgapur nor Asansol, and touch none of the OTHER three of the four (the owner's rule; src/lib/live/kolkataView.ts applies it and keeps the trains it left out, which this tab lists so that nothing is hidden unseen). A picker of the four stations is on top, each with its count; the station chosen shows its mail, express and special trains in the order of the clock AT THE STATION (the departure large, as on the other tabs), and its local and suburban trains below in violet, as on the other tabs. Each express train has its saved FARES from the station (to the end of its run, and to every stop), and the card has the same "find a fare to a station" box, limited to the trains of the station. The local trains have no fare here, and the tab says why. All of it is read from the database (src/app/api/live/railway-kol): the trains and fares were saved while the plant's paid RailRadar month lasted and are NOT refreshed, so the tab says when they were saved. It is the saved timetable, not live running status. I ask for a station's trains only when the tab is opened (RailwayTabs.tsx mounts this panel then), and again when another station is chosen. Nothing typed is sent anywhere. Sizes are in rem and the rows wrap: nothing here has a fixed pixel width, so a larger text size or a long train name changes the layout and does not break it.

behaviours: the picker has four tabs in the owner's order, each with its code, its own name and its two counts
the station chosen is the selected tab (Howrah), the others are not, and only the selected one is in the tab order
each station's counts are on its card: Howrah 4 express and 2 local, Sealdah 1 express, Santragachi 1 express and no local
the cards share the width and wrap by themselves (an auto-fit grid in rem), so a long name or a larger text size makes more rows and breaks nothing
the intro says what is listed: the trains that START at the four, do not go over Durgapur or Asansol and do not touch any other of the four; it gives the total (8 shown) and the clock
the express list has the trains of Howrah in the order of the clock at Howrah (06:05, 08:45, 09:10, 21:55), the special among them, and not the two the rule left out (13023, 12839) nor the locals
a train shows its time at the station with 'starts here' (it starts there), its name, number and class, both ends with the codes, and its days (Sahid Express: Mon, Thu)
how far and how long the whole run is a chip (1,204 km · 23 h 5 min), with a note saying what it measures

a train with a saved fare has the ₹ Fares button (12347, 12021); a train without one has none, and says why in a dashed chip: 'No fare sold' (13031, the service sold nothing), 'Fare not collected' (the special 03003, sold but not collected)
the local trains are in their own violet section: the suburban 37101 and the MEMU 63001, with the words that most of them have no fare and why
a local train that the reservation system does sell (63001, its fare is saved) has a button that says ₹ Fares, not a hint, and one that is not sold (37101) has none and no chip of 'No fare sold'
the column says how many of the express trains have saved fares: '2 of the 4 have saved fares from Howrah' (the local train with one is not counted there)
'only trains that run today' drops the Mon/Thu train (12347) on a Wednesday, and a train that runs daily stays
'Special trains' off drops the special (03003)
the next train that runs today after 10:00 is marked in its list (12347 is Mon/Thu, so the 21:55 is not; the Jan Shatabdi is gone by 10:00)
the trains the rule left out are listed in a closed disclosure, each with the other stations it touches: 13023 at Santragachi, 12839 at Santragachi and Kolkata
it says plainly that they are outside the rule, not wrong
a station with nothing left out has no such list
the line says when the timetable was saved and when the fares were received, with how long ago, green while they are young, and that nothing refreshes them
when the records are more than a week old the line turns amber and says to check NTES and IRCTC
while another station is being asked for, the picker stays with that station selected and the lists wait (a pulsing placeholder), so the old station's trains are never shown under the new name
the picker alone works as a tab list with the arrow keys (the handler is on every tab)

the tab has what the other tabs have: the two switches, the legend, the fare finder (going from Howrah), the short forms with the four stations written out, the timetable-not-live words and the NTES and RailRadar links
the fare words say the starting station: Howrah, Sealdah, Santragachi, Kolkata (and still Durgapur and Asansol for the other tabs)
the railway card has three tabs: Durgapur first and selected, then Asansol, then 'Kolkata: Howrah, Sealdah, Santragachi, Kolkata'
the Kolkata tab is not asked for until it is opened: its panel is hidden and empty
starting on the Kolkata tab shows it first (loading) and hides the Durgapur panel
the panel's title names the three places; 'sdah' opens the card on the Kolkata tab, 'asn' on Asansol, anything else on Durgapur
the words open the right tab: hwh, sealdah, santragachi, kolkata, koaa, chitpur name a Kolkata station; asn still wins over them; dgr and durgapur keep it on Durgapur; 'asn durgapur' is still Asansol
the Kolkata codes are key words (they open the card alone) and the station names are extra words (they need 'train' or another key)
the fare, stops and finder routes read the Kolkata tables only for one of the four codes (isStartCode); anything else means Durgapur, and ASN is still the Asansol tab
the Kolkata fare box never writes (its store's put does nothing), and no Kolkata route asks RailRadar
the list route reads only the station code (checked against the four, Howrah when it is anything else) and keeps no copy of its own in the database
nothing in the Kolkata tab has a pixel text size or a pixel width or height: every size is in rem or the box's own content
